A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DS2 research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and rearrangement.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations and analyses of LLM-generated ratings in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds clusterability diagnostics, an AlpaGasus comparison, resource measurements and diversity-selection experiments.

M1.justification: The four-stage DS2 procedure, score correction mechanism and quality-first/diversity-second selection remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 adds an explicit CuratedScores assignment, but this documents score correction already described in v1 rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: The five training-data sources and evaluation benchmarks are retained. The added Alpaca-only comparison and diversity experiments reuse existing datasets and tasks; their subset sizes, model configurations and metrics are protocol changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain their comparator membership. The new AlpaGasus and resource comparisons reuse previously evaluated methods; the repository checkpoint, rating model and quantization differences concern experimental settings rather than a new comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 9k-from-52k Alpaca comparison using LLaMA-2-7B with 4-bit LoRA, and top/bottom-10k diversity tests using LLaMA-3.2-3B and TruthfulQA MC2. It removes the previously stated 70B setup while retaining the main 7B/8B benchmark splits and budgets. These are targeted protocol additions and revisions, without evidence that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds score-gap distributions, embedding-distance analysis and nearest-neighbor examples examining clusterability. Appendices H and I add resource-cost comparisons and a diversity-only top-versus-bottom selection ablation. These substantially expand investigation of assumptions, practical cost and component usefulness beyond v1's retained analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the three-trial statement using different data-selection seeds in Section 5.1 and unchanged existing plots. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests; its score-gap histograms describe data distributions rather than estimation uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original benchmark tables and plots retain their results. Added findings include Figure 7's 4.1-point average advantage in the new AlpaGasus comparison, clusterability and resource measurements, and Table 17's finding that high-diversity selection helps Flan but hurts WizardLM and Alpaca. v1's numerical cross-rater overlap findings in Section 3.1 are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a binary consensus derivation explicitly invoking conditional independence, beyond v1's general consensus equations. The principal definitions and Equation 1 remain unchanged, with no new identifiability theorem. The added first-order marginalization identity omits the class-prior factor, although the subsequent binary equations include it.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: correcting LLM rating errors, combining quality with diversity, outperforming full-pool training using 3.3% of the data, and matching or surpassing LIMA. The additional experiments support existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: New limitations explicitly address sample-independent noise, textual violations of clusterability, larger model scales and stronger rating models. New discussion argues for tolerance of clusterability violations and concludes that diversity alone is not universally effective. v2 also removes the earlier interpretation connecting cross-rater overlap to pretrained knowledge similarity.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, the default confidence probability of 0.5, explicit curation pseudocode, AlpaGasus checkpoint provenance, and CPU/GPU execution and timing details. It also discloses 8-bit generation in the TruthfulQA evaluation. Most existing training hyperparameters and prompt documentation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al.'s 'Long is more for alignment' citation for the existing completion-length baseline and removes several background references, particularly on noisy labels. Its central positioning relative to AlpaGasus, DEITA and transition-matrix estimation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects wording, updates author information, adds acknowledgments, shortens some discussions and expands the appendix organization and mathematical explanations. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact; the additions do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The ICLR layout substantially rearranges displays: the pipeline moves into the introduction, Table 2 is transposed, LIMA plots are merged, and the performance-gap table becomes part of Figure 7. New diagnostic plots, example tables, resource comparisons and diversity results further expand the visual presentation; retained plots preserve their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added AlpaGasus comparison, diversity ablation and resource measurements address empirical and practical questions left open in v1, while explicit limitations and code-access information improve transparency. These are useful targeted gains, but the score-gap diagnostics use model-generated scores and do not directly validate ground-truth clusterability. The new binary derivation also introduces a missing class-prior factor, limiting its explanatory improvement.
